attBesluta.text: This AC line crimper works great! Highly recommend. I know there isn't much call for crimping AC lines anymore, but I'm installing a Vintage Air Kit in a 1962 C20 and the closest place to get AC ends crimped is 45 miles away. This is affordable and works great.

I installed a Vintage Air retrofit A/C system on my 1967 Mustang. I thought the kit would come with premade hoses, but instead came with a kit to make my own hoses. I had difficulty finding a local shop willing to make the hoses for me using the parts that came in the kit. I purchased this tool and made my own hoses. The crimps may not look quite as perfect as a premade hose, but they came out pretty good and they do not leak.

Works as advertised. Please make sure ground is soft as possible for best results--after a good soaking rain or lots of sprinkler time. The prongs go much deeper. I used heavy cinder blocks and the tray should be bigger. Turning does not tear up the yard. My only complaint is that the directions are nearly useless (common complaint). Luckily, I found a YouTube video to square things up. However, no instructions on how the wheel assembly should sit in relation to the under carriage. Had to disassemble it a time or two to get it to roll correctly with prongs off the ground or in the ground!! So aggravating!!! Vevor, make a how to assemble video for each of your products!!!
Was easy to put together, Tires were already full of air.Easy to hook up to my Tractor.All I had to do was add Cement bricks for weight
Love the areator, at first I was nervous with how many plugs it pulled, but now 2 weeks later my grass is looking better then it has in 5 years. Highly recommend

I was surprised to find a manual core aerator. I thought the only way to core aerate was to rent a big machine. This thing does the job. Note that it is a bit of a workout to push it. Also, you WILL need to fill it up with sand to increase the weight of the machine. The more sand you add the deeper the aeration, but the harder you will need to push.
Filled it with sand heavy as hell. I have a small hill and I am dripping in sweat. Use tomorrow's cardio today...

This is a very good aerator. You do need to fill it with sand or stones. Sharp turns can bend the tines. Good work out. Pros are price and easy to store and maintain. No motor to worry about. Cons are the tines can bend and it arrived missing parts ( which were replaced in 10 days, so all good)
